name: psftools
why: Tools for inspecting and editing PC Screen Font bitmaps, a neat way into a hidden binary format behind terminal text.

brief.what_it_is: PSF Tools is a set of command-line utilities for inspecting and converting simple fixed-width bitmap fonts in the PC Screen Font (PSF) format. The homepage describes it as doing for bitmap fonts what NetPBM does for images. It converts many legacy font formats into PSF (raw DOS fonts, Windows FNT/FON, Spectrum +3, MDA ROM dumps, DOS CP/CPI codepages, Hercules WOF, Wyse-60, BBC Micro, Amstrad CP/M, plain text, Berkeley vfont) and converts PSF back out to formats such as BDF, a C include file, XBM, per-character PBM, plain text, and raw. The package installs about 35 executables, named in the ams2psf, psf2bdf, raw2psf style.
brief.why_it_exists: The author wants a general toolkit for simple fixed-width bitmap fonts, modelled on NetPBM, so that fonts from many old machines and operating systems can be moved into and out of a common PSF format.
brief.how_it_works: Each converter is a separate program that reads one format and writes another, with PSF as the hub format, so a font can be moved between two non-PSF formats by chaining two tools. The homepage also describes psfxform-style edits and psfdiff, which compares two PSF files as a visual image. psfxsaa and vfontxsaa upscale fonts using the SAA5050 smoothing algorithm. The homepage does not spell out the internal design beyond this.
brief.install_notes: The homepage offers a Unix source tarball (psftools-1.1.3.tar.gz, development; psftools-1.0.14.tar.gz, stable), so Unix users build from source; the build steps were not on the homepage. Precompiled Windows x86 zips and DOS zips are also offered. To load PSF fonts into the Linux console you need the kbd package, which the homepage notes you should already have. Build and first-run steps were not seen.
brief.standout: It is a hub-and-spoke converter for a very obscure corner of computing: dozens of legacy machine font formats (Amstrad CP/M, LocoScript, BBC Micro, Hercules WriteOn, Wyse-60) all routed through one PSF format, with the author's own vfont2 proposal for round-tripping to Berkeley vfont.
brief.status: Maintained, as far as the homepage shows. The development release is 1.1.3 with a changelog entry dated 1.1.3 and the page footer reads John Elliott 2026-04-28. The stable release is 1.0.14. The exact release date of 1.1.3 was not shown, and no repository commit history was checked.
brief.caveats: Some formats are one-way or partial: the homepage lists separate to-PSF and from-PSF format lists, so not every format converts both ways. The Windows and DOS builds are precompiled binaries for those platforms only. Licence was not stated on the homepage. The tools are for simple fixed-width fonts only, not outline or proportional fonts. Only the homepage was read; no docs or source README were followed.
quotes: The PSF Tools are an attempt to do something similar to NetPBM, for simple fixed-width bitmap fonts.
[1.1.3] New utility (psfdiff) to compare two PSF files as a visual image.
[1.1.0] psf2ams: If passed an 8x16 font, the self-loading COM file now loads it at full height on the PCW16 (and scales it down on other computers).
